topic: What the Bloop, the loud mystery sound in the Pacific, really was
hook: Something in the Pacific made a sound.

scenes.narration: It was 1997. Researchers were listening for underwater volcanic activity in the southern Pacific. Then their hydrophones picked up something else.
It was strange. It was powerful. Hydrophones more than 3,219 kilometres apart heard it. It earned a name. The Bloop.
Then came the guesses. Secret military exercises. Ship engines. Whales. A giant squid. Or a sea creature unknown to science.
But the answer took eight years to find. And it was not alive.
Scientists at NOAA's Pacific Marine Environmental Laboratory kept listening. They moved their hydrophones ever closer to Antarctica. Following the sound. South.
In 2005, they found it. The Bloop was an icequake. An iceberg, cracking and breaking away from an Antarctic glacier.
No monster. No secret weapon. Just ice, loud enough to be heard across the Pacific. And about 95 percent of the ocean is still unexplored.

loop_line: So listen closely. Somewhere out there, the ice is still breaking. And something in the Pacific is making a sound.
title: The Bloop: the ocean's mystery sound, solved
description: Source: What is the Bloop? NOAA National Ocean Service, Ocean Facts.
